title: The Bouncer (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal cricket storytelling
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Now there are polite ways to greet a batsman
And then there's the bouncer
The bouncer doesn't knock on the door
The bouncer comes through the window at head height
And waits to see what you do about that

[Verse 2]
A good bouncer is not about aggression
It's a question
Are you still here?
Are you still thinking?
Or are you already somewhere else?

[Chorus]
The bouncer says — good morning
The bouncer says — how do you do
The bouncer says — I know where you're standing
Do you know what I'm about to do

[Bridge]
Every batsman has a weakness up around the ears
A memory of a pitch they've seen before
The bouncer doesn't ask for your opinion
The bouncer is the knock you've been waiting for

[Verse 3]
Chas would watch the short ball with a quiet eye
Said — son, the bouncer's never about fury
It's about information
It's about watching what a man does
When the ball's already past the place he thought it was going

[Outro]
That's the bouncer
That's my boy
